messages:
sam (support): FYI customer PROD-4423 — they asked for a one-time downtime credit but our platform prorated the subscription instead. Bad UX, billing affected. Logs attached.

router-bot: auto-router decision -> prorate_subscription (confidence=0.61); candidate tools: [create_one_time_credit (0.34), prorate_subscription (0.61)].

harper (eng): ugh, looks like an alias collision in tool registry. Both tools expose alias 'apply_credit' and router picks based on fuzzy intent + schema match. Repro steps below.

harper (eng): repro: prompt: "Please credit our account for two hours of downtime" -> router picks prorate_subscription. curl to decision endpoint:
```
POST /v1/router/decide
{ "prompt": "credit account for two hours of downtime", "context": {"account_id":"acct_9"} }
```
response: ```{ "selected_tool":"prorate_subscription", "confidence":0.61, "tool_call": {"subscription_id":"sub_123","effective_date":"2026-03-16","percentage":-8 }}```

noah (sre): Did prorate actually execute? Any 4xx/5xx? Or did it succeed and mutate billing state?

harper (eng): It executed (200) and created a negative prorate adjustment — invoice totals changed and taxes recalculated. create_one_time_credit did not get called. Customer unhappy. :facepalm:

harper (eng): Root cause: both tool aliases include 'credit' token. Router scoring currently uses intent embedding similarity + basic schema match, but we don't penalize negative/one-off semantics. The prorate schema accepts a free-text 'reason' and an optional 'percentage' so fuzzy match favored it.

taylor (ml): Quick mitigation: 1) blacklist alias overlap for billing-critical tools, 2) add schema-awareness to prefer tools that require an explicit 'amount_cents' field when prompt mentions explicit money terms, 3) bump alias weight for create_one_time_credit. I'll open a patch.

harper (eng): I'll push a routing-table hotfix to remove the shared alias and add a unit test. Also scheduling a rollback window.

noah (sre): Please add an alert that flags billing-tool runs where selected_tool != highest_money_schema_score and confidence < 0.75 so support can catch these fast.

sam (support): thanks — I've messaged the customer with an apology and explained we're reversing the prorate and issuing a one-time credit. Ticket updated with repro and link to this thread.

harper (eng): Patch queued to prod in next 30m. Will follow up with test logs.

taylor (ml): Follow-up ML work: incorporate schema-field importance into the affordance scorer (amount_cents, invoice_id, subscription_id semantics).

sam (support): closing loop — will mark as resolved once credit is issued and invoice corrected. :white_check_mark:
